chapter.chaptertitle: Record of Care, Treatment, and Services Chapter

titles.title: The organization maintains complete and accurate clinical records.
Entries in the clinical record are authenticated.
Documentation in the clinical record is entered in a timely manner.
The organization audits its clinical records.
The clinical record contains information that reflects the resident's care, treatment, and services.
The clinical record contains documentation of the use of restraint.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to the activities program at least quarterly.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to nutrition care services at least quarterly.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to nursing care.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to medical treatment and care, and changes in the resident�s condition.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to rehabilitation services.
Clinical record documentation includes the provision of and response to social services.
Clinical record documentation includes resident education.
Treatment provided to the resident by external resources is documented in the clinical record.
Effects of medications on residents, and associated pharmacist evaluation and physician consultation, are documented in the clinical record.
Qualified staff receive and record verbal orders.
The organization documents the resident�s discharge information.

notes.note: Note 1: Authentication can be verified through electronic signatures, written signatures or initials, rubber-stamp signatures, or computer key.

Note 2: For paper-based records, signatures entered for purposes of authentication after transcription or for verbal orders are dated when required by law or regulation or organization policy. For electronic records, electronic signatures will be date-stamped.
Note: In determining the frequency of preparing a summary of the residents condition, consideration should be given to residents with complex needs or short lengths of stay.
